– Lenco Armored Vehicles, the leading manufacturer of armored vehicles for law enforcement, fire and rescue, and government agencies worldwide, today announced a $5 million investment in new machinery and facility improvements at its Pittsfield, Massachusetts headquarters.

The investment includes the installation of a state-of-the-art fiber laser CNC machine and two precision press brakes. The new equipment leverages the latest cutting, forming, and bending technology, significantly increasing Lenco’s production output while enabling the creation of more complex and sophisticated vehicle components.
Lenco’s mission has always been to provide the highest quality armored vehicles to agencies that depend on us,” said Lenny Light, Executive Vice President
, Lenco Armored Vehicles. “This investment reflects our commitment to innovation, improved production efficiency, and ensuring that BearCats are delivered to customers as quickly as possible.”
Expanding Production Capacity and Capabilities

The fiber laser also allows Lenco to conduct rapid prototyping and bring certain component production in-house that previously required suppliers. This expanded capability supports redesigns of legacy parts to improve usability and opens opportunities to integrate new technologies into future BearCat vehicles.

The investment has already created approximately five new positions across engineering, production, and facilities to program, operate, and support the new equipment. Beyond direct job creation, the fiber laser purchased is one of the largest machines of its type in the country, adding unique advanced manufacturing capabilities to western Massachusetts.

With support from local partners such as the Berkshire Innovation Center and Mass Tech, Lenco’s investment contributes to the region’s growth in advanced manufacturing while strengthening the company’s role as one of Berkshire County’s leading manufacturers.
Facility Improvements and Long-Term Strategy

While Lenco’s fabrication department will see the most direct impact from these upgrades, downstream processes such as coatings and mechanical assembly will also benefit. The increase in consistency of cut and formed parts improves fit-up and assembly as each vehicle moves through production.
The project began in September 2024 and was completed in December 2025.
